decision: Zero or more namespace body elements, exactly as KerML 8.2.3.4.1 states it. This is the start symbol of the KerML grammar: a .kerml file is a sequence of namespace members, aliases and imports with no enclosing declaration, and an empty file is a valid root namespace.
notes:
THIS IS THE KERML VARIANT (ADR-0014). SysML states RootNamespace with a different body, PackageBodyElement*, which is not a defect on either side: the two languages admit different members at the root. That variant is a separate unit and is not consulted here.

The clause and KerML.xtext agree. The Xtext writes `{SysML::Namespace}NamespaceBodyElement*`; the braces are an Xtext action that creates the Namespace object before any member is parsed, so that an empty file still yields one. That is abstract-syntax construction and is not carried into the rule.

The clause's note 1 is why this production is the start symbol: every element other than a root namespace is contained in one, so every valid KerML text parses from here.

NO KEYWORD AND NULLABLE, so nothing about a file's first token identifies it as a root namespace. It is identified by being the whole file.

evidence.note: states RootNamespace as NamespaceBodyElement*, with note 1 making it the start of every KerML text
the same body behind a {SysML::Namespace} object-creation action
the file is one root namespace whose single member is `package Classes { ... }`
